title: Fantasy Premier League
text:
The Beautiful Game
This is my journey of playing FPL with 0 ball knowledge and a bit of Python knowledge.

title: Preseason
text:
The Goal
The purpose of this project is to see how well I can perform using a systematic set of trading rules based on historical data, rather than any knowledge or experience of football

title: Preseason
text:
The Goalposts
What does “performing well” mean? The most natural measure of performance is percentile rank among all FPL players, but that doesn’t have an objective benchmark. Is 50% good? 33%?
Perhaps the most objective measure of my performance is the difference between my final point score and the score I would have ended on if I had made no transfers throughout the season. This will evaluate the quality of my transfer decisions, but not of my initial choice of squad. I think I am happy with this, because I expect my initial squad to be far from both the best and worst initial squad.
Since my evaluation method is essentially controlling for the initial squad choice, once the season is over I might be able to work out how well my initial squad would have done with 0 transfers, compared to all the other possibilities.

title: Preseason
text:
Relegation zone
That leaves me with a baseline target of ensuring my final points is higher than the points my initial squad would have ended up on. With 37 transfers

title: Preseason
text:
Promotion zone
A target that feels certainly ambitious and objective (although, impossible to gauge if at all realistic) target might be to end on more than 1.5x the points that my initial squad would have

title: Preseason
text:
Safe zone
Ending up in the Relegation Zone will be an embarrassing but fun story to tell. Ending up in the Promotion Zone will be an even more fun story to tell. If both elude me, then at least I will have the code for my CV.

title: Preseason
text:
Formation
How should I choose when to buy, sell, and hold players? And on the basis of what data? I will be using moving averages to make my decisions. I will aim to buy players who are perform well over the last 3 weeks, and vice versa for selling. I will not waste my transfers transacting on averagely performing players, meaning I might not buy good players who are not good enough, and might not sell (i.e. will hold) players who are not (yet) performing badly enough.

title: Preseason
text:
Financial fairplay
I will only be using data available from the official FPL API. More specifically, I’ll only be using data pertaining to players’ points scored in the current and past two seasons. I will not make any decisions based on qualitative or other quantitative data I receive in any form or via any means, external to the API. Secondarily, this means I am not “cheating”. Primarily, this is because I have no reason to believe I’ll be able to employ this information better than that from the API.

title: Preseason
text:
Pitch limits
Currently undecided if I want to use chips. I think if I do, I will resign myself to using them the week before they expire, or not at all, on the basis that if I am going to use them, I should use them when I have the most information to hand. But, I don’t think I’ll use them, because it’ll make it very difficult to compare my performance with my initial squad’s. I would have to work out how I would have used them, had I kept my initial squad, which feels like a lot of work.

title: GW 1 - The Initial Squad
text:
The Initial Squad
Before I choose which players I want, how do I choose how many of each position I want, subject to the maximum constraints? I’ll decide based on the average points scored for each position, over the last season:


Mean Goalkeeper Points over last season: 72
Mean Defender Points over last season: 74
Mean Midfielder Points over last season: 70
Mean Forward Points over last season: 70
Mean Goalkeeper cost: 4.8
Mean Defender cost: 4.8
Mean Midfielder cost: 5.6
Mean Forward cost: 6.1


So, very crudely, Defenders are a bit more lucrative than other positions, and the opposite for Forwards. So I’ll pick two Goalkeeprs, then as many Defenders as I can, then as many Midfielders as I can, and then as few Forwards as I can. Perhaps this formation will change as the season progresses, depending on whether relative points/cost changes between different positions. I also will use as a tiebreaker a preference to add players from teams not already in my squad, to hopefully reduce the variance of my weekly points.
Below, we’ll order players by the ratio of their points over the last two seasons, divided by their current cost. I’ll then select for my initial squad players with a high ratio and a low cost.The idea is that I’m happy to buy underpriced players who score fewer points, so that I have the flexibility later in the season to use current season data to make transfers. Currently, I’m picking based on prior season performance, which it feels fair to assume is uniformly a worse indicator for future performance than current season data.
As we only have current cost, which is a dynamic field, the tables below are likely to show different players than the ones I chose at the time of writing. But, the logic is the same.

title: GW 1 - The Initial Squad
text:
Leftover Capital
This leaves me with £14m to play with. If I make 38 transfers over the season, I can average a net cost of ~£0.5m per transfer. The idea is that every transfer I make will use some capital to improve my team made from old data, on the basis of new data (current season data). I expect my initial squad to optimal with respect to the old data (as far as my selection logic is concerned), but to be a very poor predictor of this season’s performance when compared with current season data, as it eventually emerges. Selecting a cheap initial squad gives me flexiblity to leverage current season data to make “corrections” to my initial squad that was chosen from old data.
